newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SKODA SHARES RATED A SELL BY ABN-AMRO.
newsitem.headline: SKODA SHARES RATED A SELL BY ABN-AMRO.

text.p: Shares in Czech engineering group Skoda a.s., which makes products ranging from beverage cans to nuclear machinery, should under-perform the market and are rated a sell by bank ABN-Amro in a recent report to investors.
In the report, dated October 1, ABN's Emerging Markets Investment Research team said that a lack of information concerning many of the firm's recent takeovers and deals also cloud its outlook.
It said that Skoda's price of 1,070 crowns as of October 1 make the issue a sell.
"We feel at current levels Skoda's valuation is stretched and expect them to under-perform the market as a whole," the report said.
Several of Skoda's divisions have recently signed deals to produce everything from trucks in Bulgaria to power plant equipment for Serbia and a wide array of goods in China.
The report said that while these deals could be beneficial for Skoda, "too little is yet known to justify taking a positive view on the company's future".

"The company still lacks a fully-fledged management information system which, against the background of a myriad of subsidiaries and associated companies located across the globe, makes the company extremely difficult to manage," it said.
"Combined with the often poor financial condition of the new acquisitions, we question the positive outlook as maintained by Skoda management," the report concluded.
Skoda, the largest engineering concern in the Czech Republic, is no longer affiliated with car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s., now a unit of Germany's Volkswagen AG.
